name: Aggression
summary: Hitting, kicking, biting, throwing objects, or other outward aggressive acts, most often arising from frustration, communication breakdown, or sensory/emotional overwhelm rather than intent to harm.
triggers: Inability to communicate a need or discomfort verbally
Disruption to routine or a forced, abrupt transition
Being denied a wanted item or activity
Fatigue, hunger, or illness lowering frustration tolerance

remedies.text: Functional behavior assessment (FBA) with a qualified clinician to identify what the aggression is communicating before choosing a strategy
Functional communication training — teaching words, signs, or a communication device to request breaks, help, or wanted items instead of using aggression
Reduce known triggers proactively (advance warning of transitions, quiet space available) rather than only reacting after aggression occurs
Regular physical activity to support emotional regulation and reduce baseline stress

sources.label: Autism Research Institute - Strategies for Addressing Challenging Behaviors
